key_insight: A continuous-time policy gradient framework learns from discrete observations, with exponential convergence proved for an entropy-regularized policy flow.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports control learning under unknown stochastic dynamics while preserving the continuous-time structure of the problem.
method: Derive a performance difference lemma and policy gradients for randomized and parametrized policies.
Bound discrete-update convergence by critic error, policy-regression error, and learning step size.
Use PhiBE to construct a surrogate generator from discrete transitions for on-policy and off-policy actor-critic algorithms.
evidence_signal: Experiments on an entropy-regularized linear-quadratic regulator and a nonlinear wheeled robot evaluate performance and stability with known and data-driven dynamics.
watch_item: The exponential convergence result applies to the idealized regularized policy flow; discrete implementations must account for critic error, policy-regression error, and step size.
paper_title: Continuous-Time Policy Gradient from Discrete Data: Convergence Analysis and Model-Free Algorithms
